Without `sandbox`, the page inside an `iframe` can run scripts, submit forms, open popups, and navigate your page away. `sandbox=""` turns all of that off, and each `allow-*` word turns one thing back on.

The rule reports:

- an `iframe` that has no `sandbox` attribute
- a word in `sandbox` that is not a known permission, such as a typo
- `allow-scripts` together with `allow-same-origin`. With both, a page from your own origin can remove the `sandbox` attribute from its own `iframe`.

It checks `<iframe>` and `React.createElement("iframe", ...)`. A value that is not a string literal, such as `sandbox={permissions}`, is not checked.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
const map = <iframe src="https://maps.example.com" />;

const video = <iframe src="https://video.example.com" sandbox="allow-everything" />;

const widget = <iframe src="/widget" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" />;
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import React from "react";

const map = React.createElement("iframe", { src: "https://maps.example.com" });
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const map = <iframe src="https://maps.example.com" sandbox="" />;

const video = <iframe src="https://video.example.com" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-popups" />;

const widget = <iframe src="/widget" sandbox={permissions} />;
```
